observations: A rounded form fills most of the olive-green field, outlined in thick black with a jagged fringe of short dark marks running along its lower edge.
The left socket holds a large spiral in blue and white lines coiling inward; the right socket contains a smaller lobed shape in red and orange on a white ground.
Yellow dash-marks cluster along the left side, cyan bar-marks stack on the right, and magenta scribbles cross the lower half, all layered over a yellow-green interior.
reading: Two mismatched sockets—one a wide blue spiral, one a compact red-orange rosette—sit inside a rounded form that reads as a mask. The asymmetry feels less like damage than like two different ways of looking. Dense layering of yellow dashes, cyan bars, and magenta scrawl gives the surface a crowded, restless quality, while the open black mouth below pulls the eye downward into something rawer.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, the disc-and-fringe structure here echoes the circular form in title-neighbor nnxyz nnotb #179, though #179 surrounds its disc with a dense field of blue and gold marks rather than the plain olive ground seen here.

connections.reason: Both works center a circular disc-like form with a fringed or patterned border, but #179 fills the surrounding field with repeating small marks while #178 leaves it as flat olive ground.

lookingQuestion: What does the size difference between the two socket forms—the wide blue spiral and the smaller red rosette—do to how you move between the left and right sides of the image?
ambiguities: The lobed shape in the right socket could be read as a flower or an eye; neither reading is confirmed by the image alone.
